genericProblem: A UI consumer can have a source vector and a screen-level baseline record but still enter focused or L2 verification without proving every user-visible control, state, cascade, owner boundary and accessibility assertion against its accepted IA.

counterexamples.reason: A five-source prewrite receipt proves only that the prescribed sources were reread; it neither proves the control mapping nor authorizes L2.
Compilation and mechanical scans cannot establish user task, control cascade, opaque public boundary, or owner readback semantics.
A nine-dimension screen record is an index, not evidence that every visible component and state satisfies the IA sheet.

findings.genericProblem: The current U03 baseline was marked PASS before an explicit per-control implementation comparison was recorded, so it cannot be used as the L2 admission fact.
findings.minimalRepair: Keep the existing prewrite baseline as a source-read admission only, add a distinct control-level final-alignment record for every physical consumer, require that record only becomes PASS after all rows pass, and make the joint L2 runner reject any other state.

findings.genericProblem: Public login/recovery controls can visually resemble their IA while omitting required dynamic page titles, owner-only test-code display, opaque errors, or stale legacy reset entry removal.
findings.minimalRepair: For every public/auth consumer, compare exact control copy/shape, source/readback, enablement and reset cascade, loading/error state, session prohibition, testId/accessibility and legacy path absence before focused proof.

preventionDispositions.reason: The existing UI-IA admission and existing joint runner will consume the explicit final baseline status and reject non-PASS.
Control-level semantics require source-and-code comparison; the package exit and independent review must replay the finite rows.

controlComparisonRequired.l2Admission: All required rows must be PASS; static/type/focused proof remain distinct from business and cleanup results.
